talks.title: Agent Loops, Decoded: Fundamentals to Agentic Patterns in Spring AI
talks.abstract: This talk introduces Spring AI agents as context orchestrators, starting with ChatClient, memory, Advisors, RAG, Tool Calling, and MCP. It then builds advanced agent patterns: tool discovery, evaluation loops, explainable agents, planning, user questioning, subagents, and agent-to-agent integration, previewing Spring AI 2.1’s typed multi-step agent abstraction.

video.title: Agent Loops, Decoded: Fundamentals to Agentic Patterns in Spring AI  by  Christian Tzolov

talks.title: From AI to Agent: A Field Guide to Agentic Patterns in LangChain4j
talks.abstract: This talk shows how to evolve a Java AI app from simple LLM calls into controllable agentic systems. It covers sequential, loop, parallel, and conditional workflows, shared state, supervisors, planners, human checkpoints, and observability—helping you decide when to use workflows versus autonomous agents.

video.title: From AI to Agent: A Field Guide to Agentic Patterns in LangChain4j  by  Loïc Magnette

talks.title: From Autocomplete to Autopilot: How AI Is Changing the Developer Experience
talks.abstract: This talk explores the rise of agentic workflows and context engineering in AI-assisted development. Using GitHub Copilot’s latest tools, it shows how teams delegate end-to-end tasks, from architecture scaffolding to PRs, and how developers, SREs, DevOps, and PMs shift from writing code to expressing intent.

video.title: From Autocomplete to Autopilot: How AI Is Changing the Developer Experience by Tugdual Grall

talks.title: Prompt It Right: Spring Boot Testing in the AI Era
talks.abstract: This 3-hour session teaches Spring Boot testing across the full testing pyramid—unit, sliced, and integration tests with Testcontainers—so you can guide AI to generate useful tests, spot misleading ones, avoid common pitfalls, and improve your test suite with practical patterns and quick wins.

video.title: Prompt It Right: Spring Boot Testing in the AI Era by Philip Riecks

talks.title: Solving Multimodal and Long-Context Challenges
talks.abstract: This deep-dive explores extending LLMs with multimodal and long-context capabilities to solve real-world tasks. It presents step-by-step Python notebook solutions for video transcription with speaker identification, large-scale knowledge graph generation, image automation, and visual object detection, restoration, and editing.

video.title: Solving Multimodal and Long Context Challenges by Laurent Picard

talks.title: 🚀 From Java to AI: Build Your First Intelligent Agent System!
talks.abstract: Hands-on workshop on building production-grade AI in Java with LangChain4j. Learn CDI-based AI injection, conversational memory, function calling, declarative agent workflows, and the Supervisor Pattern. Gain practical patterns, MCP/A2A protocol knowledge, and skills to integrate robust AI agents into enterprise architectures.

talks.title: Java is for Data Science, Too: Building an End-to-End ML Pipeline Without Leaving the JVM
talks.abstract: This practical session shows how Java can handle end-to-end data science without switching to Python. Using JTaccuino, Hardwood, dflib, DeepNetts, and a new plotting API, participants will build a complete predictive machine learning pipeline in Java, from data exploration to visualization and neural network training.

talks.title: Destructoring is the future of Javas Encapsulation
talks.abstract: Project Amber’s “Derived Record/Class Creation” aims to make object deconstruction and reconstruction first-class in Java, fixing serialization’s encapsulation issues. It enables safer, more robust serialization, plus withers and broader pattern matching support for records and normal classes.

video.title: Destructoring is the future of Javas Encapsulation  by  Richard Gross

talks.title: Introduction to Spring AI
talks.abstract: Spring AI helps developers bring generative AI into Spring Boot applications. This session covers building blocks like chat, RAG, tool calling, testing, observability, and agentic AI patterns with MCP, showing how to create production-ready AI applications and agentic systems through hands-on examples.

video.title: Introduction to Spring AI by Timo Salm

talks.title: Java, LEGO & AI: Teaching the Next Generation to Build, Not Just Prompt
talks.abstract: This session shows why teaching programming still matters in the AI era, using LEGO SPIKE robots in Java-based workshops for children. It covers technical methods to control SPIKE with Java, challenges encountered, educational lessons learned, and includes live robot demos.

video.title: Java, LEGO & AI: Teaching the Next Generation to Build, Not Just Prompt  by Eddy Vos

talks.title: Building Autonomous AI Agents with Spring
talks.abstract: This workshop teaches building autonomous agentic AI systems with Java, Spring AI, and MCP. It covers prompting, chat memory, RAG, tool integration, and agentic patterns, plus production concerns like observability, security, and reliability. Attendees will create a multi-agent system for complex tasks.

talks.title: Can AI Build a Jakarta EE Runtime? The Vidocq Experiment
talks.abstract: A candid retrospective on building a Jakarta EE Core Profile and MicroProfile runtime from scratch. It covers architectural tradeoffs, JPMS-driven design changes, CDI event lessons, spec interpretation, dependency minimization, governance decisions, and what they would do differently with JDK 25 and hindsight.

video.title: Can AI Build a Jakarta EE Runtime? The Vidocq Experiment by Antoine Sabot Durand, yann Blazart, Seba

talks.title: Codepocalypse Now: LangChain4j vs JetBrains Koog
talks.abstract: A live Java showdown builds the same AI agent twice using JetBrains Koog and LangChain4j. Across six coding rounds, the speakers compare memory, tool calling, workflows, guardrails, and observability, exposing different design philosophies. The audience votes on which framework best fits real agent development.

video.title: Codepocalypse Now: LangChain4j vs JetBrains Koog  by Viktor Gamov, Baruch Sadogursky

talks.title: From Developer to Builder: A Spec-Driven Development Deep Dive
talks.abstract: Spec-Driven Development uses specifications, not prompts, to guide AI coding agents. This deep dive shows how to build and evolve applications by writing specs, generating code, testing against requirements, and updating specs when needs change. It covers harness design, practical use, limits, and adoption on your own stack.

video.title: From Developer to Builder: A Spec Driven Development Deep Dive by Simon Martinelli

talks.title: Modern Java in Practice - The Features That Matter
talks.abstract: A deep dive into recent Java releases, highlighting key features like pattern matching, virtual threads, structured concurrency, new APIs, performance and security improvements, plus upcoming proposals such as value types and string templates. The talk helps developers maximize modern Java and justify upgrading.

video.title: Modern Java in Practice   The Features That Matter by   Nicolai Parlog, Falk Sippach

talks.title: The Quarkus advantage: Turning build-time metaprogramming into runtime performances
talks.abstract: The talk shows how Quarkus uses build-time indexing and bytecode generation to replace reflection-heavy Java framework mechanisms, improving startup, memory, latency, and throughput. Case studies in JSON serialization, REST clients, and LangChain4j demonstrate double-digit performance gains and the power of ahead-of-time metaprogramming.

video.title: The Quarkus advantage: Turning build time metaprogramming into runtime performances by Mario Fusco,

talks.title: Using Structured Concurrency and Scoped Values to Create a Virtual Threads Based Asynchronous Application
talks.abstract: A hands-on lab on Project Loom’s virtual threads, structured concurrency, and scoped values. It teaches building a scalable web app, parallelizing requests, passing sensitive data safely, and comparing Loom’s thread-per-request approach with reactive programming for similar throughput.

talks.title: Expanding Vector Search Beyond Similarity
talks.abstract: This session shows how to build an e-commerce vector search app with Micronaut, LangChain4j, and GraalVM. It covers embedding generation, blending similarity with business and location data, key Micronaut features, and Native Image deployment to create smarter, practical search.

video.title: Expanding Vector Search Beyond Similarity by Alina Yurenko

talks.title: From Install to Insight: A Hands-On GPU Lab for Java Developers
talks.abstract: Hands-on lab to set up a local GPU-backed LLM in Java using GPULlama3.java, TornadoVM, and DevoxxGenie. Participants install, configure, run, profile, and debug GPU acceleration with TornadoInsight, TornadoPulse, and TornadoViz, gaining a working local inference setup and practical tooling experience.

talks.title: Secure Your Coding Agent Like It’s Malware
talks.abstract: Coding agents can be easily compromised through prompt injection, file access, and tool misuse, leading to persistence or data exfiltration. Built-in sandboxes are insufficient. This talk maps key threats, explains seven defense layers, and recommends externally enforced controls like VMs and firewalls to reduce an agent’s blast radius.

video.title: Secure Your Coding Agent Like It’s Malware by Richard Gross

talks.title: The day we stopped publishing Kafka event from our API...
talks.abstract: We solved database-Kafka dual writes in our Order API by adopting a simplified Outbox pattern with Debezium, using the Order table as the outbox. This removed Kafka-specific code, reduced errors, improved robustness, and enabled a looser, more extensible event-driven architecture with key Debezium stability practices.

video.title: The day we stopped publishing Kafka event from our API     by Virginie Zinck

talks.title: Wiring Up the AI Mesh: Building A2A-Compliant Java Agents
talks.abstract: LangChain4j-CDI brings generative AI to Jakarta EE/MicroProfile with a CDI extension for easy AI service injection. It demonstrates building enterprise AI agents using MCP and A2A protocols, plus resilience, observability, and multi-provider configuration. Live coding shows deployment on Quarkus, WildFly, and Helidon in minutes.

talks.title: Your AI Agent Trusts Strangers. Let Me Show You.
talks.abstract: This session exposes indirect prompt injection in Java AI agents, showing how poisoned content can hijack trusted inputs and trigger harmful tool actions. In 30 minutes, attendees will learn to reproduce the attack, apply effective mitigations, and build a practical threat model in LangChain4j.

video.title: Your AI Agent Trusts Strangers  Let Me Show You   by  Elder Moraes

talks.title: Beyond Code: The Intent-Driven IDE for the Agentic Age
talks.abstract: This session explores intent-driven development environments where specifications guide autonomous agents in parallel workspaces. Through a live demo, it shows a task moving from spec to pull request, plus custom workflow extension. It also examines architecture, automation, context management, model choices, and the developer’s evolving role.

video.title: Beyond Code: The Intent Driven IDE for the Agentic Age by Bruno Borges

talks.title: In the loop, not in the dark: staying in control in the era of dark software factories
talks.abstract: Groma.md is an open-source tool that maintains a live architectural blueprint of your codebase, keeping you in control while agents write code. Unlike task tracking, it shows how the system evolves in real time. The talk will demo mapping a large repository into a Groma blueprint live.

video.title: In the loop, not in the dark: staying in control in the era of dark software factories  by Alex Gavr

talks.title: Stopping AI-Generated Architectural Drift: Deterministic Guardrails for Agentic Coding
talks.abstract: This talk explains how to prevent AI-generated code from spreading architectural violations by using layered guardrails. It shows why natural-language rules fail, and how deterministic enforcement with ArchUnit, custom linters, and CI gates can stop bad patterns immediately and make higher-level rules effective.

video.title: Stopping AI Generated Architectural Drift: Deterministic Guardrails for Agentic Coding by Sasha Podl

talks.title: Teaching a New Dog Old Tricks: Give the Agent a Debugger
talks.abstract: IntelliJ IDEA’s debugger tools let coding agents inspect runtime state without altering source code. Using logpoints, agents can trace behavior in running code, including compiled third-party libraries, and link output back to its origin. The debugger skill guides agents to investigate bugs more cleanly than print statements.

video.title: Teaching a New Dog Old Tricks: Give the Agent a Debugger  by  Anton Arhipov

talks.title: Building the Trusted Agent Ecosystem
talks.abstract: The session presents a Trusted Agent Ecosystem framework to address user trust barriers in the Agentic Web. Using Confidential Computing and Binary Transparency, it secures tools, inference, and remote agents via verifiable WebAssembly sandboxes and Confidential GPUs, enabling developers to build trusted agentic services.

video.title: Building the Trusted Agent Ecosystem by Ivan Petrov, Patrick McGrath

talks.title: One tool to rule them all: bash, a tiny LLM, and the birth of a coding agent
talks.abstract: A live demo shows how a tiny local LLM becomes a coding agent using just a bash tool and a simple loop. It explores tool calls, prompt engineering, error recovery, and why one built-in tool can outperform many servers—revealing how coding agents work under the hood.

video.title: One tool to rule them all: bash, a tiny LLM, and the birth of a coding agent  by  Philippe Charrièr

talks.title: Testing Architecture Made Simple
talks.abstract: The session shows how ArchUnit turns architectural decisions into automated tests, and how Taikai extends it with ready-made rules for popular technologies. Together, they help teams enforce consistent architecture, best practices, and long-term maintainability from the start.

video.title: Testing Architecture Made Simple by Gunter Rotsaert

talks.title: Hi, Belgian Java Community, we want to meet you!
talks.abstract: An informal, interactive session introducing BeJUG, Belgium’s Java User Group. Learn how it connects Java enthusiasts, what events it runs, and how to get involved as attendee, speaker, or contributor. No slides or agenda—just networking, ideas, and community discussion for all Java lovers.

talks.title: LangChain4j Community BOF
talks.abstract: An open BOF session on LangChain4j’s evolution, adoption, challenges, and roadmap. Join community members to discuss real-world use, share feedback, ask questions, and help shape the future of this fast-growing Java framework for integrating large language models.

talks.title: Building AI Agents from First Principles
talks.abstract: This workshop explains agentic AI from first principles, evolving a simple request/response flow into a full plan-act-observe-decide loop. Using Spring Boot/Spring AI examples, it covers tools, planning, memory, multi-step execution, evaluation, error handling, and termination, emphasizing robust software architecture over prompt engineering.

video.title: Building AI Agents from First Principles  by Adib Saikali

talks.title: Cheaper or Better? The Strategic Choice Behind AI Adoption
talks.abstract: This session examines two AI adoption strategies: efficiency gains or customer value creation. It explores how incentives, metrics, and workflows can lead teams to automate broken processes or improve outcomes. Participants will learn to distinguish cost-cutting AI from value-driven AI and ask better strategic questions.

video.title: Cheaper or Better? The Strategic Choice Behind AI Adoption  by Miriam Sasse

talks.title: From code to control: master deployments with Feature Flagging and OpenFeature
talks.abstract: This workshop shows how to add a feature to a Java/Angular app using feature flags with OpenFeature. It covers safe releases, error handling, A/B testing, progressive rollouts, targeting, and observability—helping teams decouple deployment from activation and ship faster with less risk.

talks.title: Learning modern Java the playful way
talks.abstract: This session introduces modern Java features like Structured Concurrency and Stream Gatherers, making them approachable for beginners and experienced developers alike. Marit and Piotr will explain the concepts and demonstrate how to use them in your IDE, helping you confidently start using modern Java tools.

video.title: Learning modern Java the playful way  by Marit van Dijk, Piotr Przybyl

talks.title: Loop Engineering, beyond prompt, context, and harness engineering
talks.abstract: This session introduces “Loop Engineering,” where developers build automated systems that steer coding agents autonomously. It covers core primitives, loop architectures, and safety practices for creating self-driving workflows that investigate, implement, and verify code, replacing manual prompting with robust AI-driven automation.

video.title: Loop Engineering, beyond prompt, context, and harness engineering  by  Guillaume Laforge, Wietse Ven

talks.title: Will Valhalla Fix Tony's Billion-Dollar Mistake?
talks.abstract: Java 28’s Valhalla project introduces preview value classes, enabling JVM optimizations like stack scalarization and heap flattening. The talk explores compatibility, revised Java semantics, nullability, construction behavior, performance, type safety, and new coding patterns, while outlining future Valhalla enhancements.

video.title: Will Valhalla Fix Tony's Billion Dollar Mistake? by José Paumard, Remi Forax

talks.title: 👩‍💻 Developing with AI: What if it were as simple as adding a library? 🧑‍💻
talks.abstract: Workshop on integrating generative AI into Java applications using tools like LangChain4j and Quarkus. Covers prompt engineering, RAG, tool calling (MCP), and agents, with a ready-to-use EasyLab environment for hands-on learning.

talks.title: Beyond system.out.println: Applying a Debugging Mindset at Scale
talks.abstract: This talk explores debugging elusive, intermittent failures in large microservice and distributed systems. It argues for a shift from traditional logging and local debugging to structured observability, using tools like OpenTelemetry and Grafana to uncover root causes and gain deeper system insight.

talks.title: From Developer to Story Builder: Engineering a Novel, an ARG, and a Transmedia World with AI
talks.abstract: A technical case study on using software-engineering practices to co-author a novel with AI. It covers context engineering, spec-driven workflows, role separation, governance to prevent drift, automated publishing, and an ARG extension, offering practical methods for managing long-running AI creative projects while preserving human authorship.

video.title: From Developer to Story Builder: Engineering a Novel, an ARG, and a Transmedia World with AI  by Rap

talks.title: Measuring the Unmeasurable: Evaluating Generative AI in Practice
talks.abstract: This session explores how to evaluate generative AI systems reliably despite their unpredictability. Using a RAG chatbot case study, it covers adapting metrics for accuracy, coherence, and business value; the limits of traditional and LLM-as-a-judge methods; the role of human review; and continuous monitoring for drift.

video.title: Measuring the Unmeasurable: Evaluating Generative AI in Practice  by Erin Pacquetet

talks.title: AI Security Deep Dive, Securing Agents and AI Applications
talks.abstract: This session covers AI security for agentic coding and AI-powered apps, including risks like prompt injection, tool abuse, poisoned retrieval, and memory manipulation. It emphasizes practical defenses, architectural patterns, and security tooling, with live demos and real-world examples to help build and use AI systems more securely.

video.title: AI Security Deep Dive, Securing Agents and AI Applications  by  Brian Vermeer

talks.title: Beyond the Chatbox: Ship On-Device AI in Your Browser
talks.abstract: This lab shows how to replace chat-style AI with real-time, on-device browser inference. Participants compare JVM backend pose estimation with in-browser WebGPU models, then build live camera overlays and measure latency. They leave with a working project, extra labs, and a framework for choosing cloud vs. device AI.

talks.title: Don’t burn your fingers in the heat of the AI (r)evolution. (And get an OpenClaw).
talks.abstract: The talk explores how to make agentic AI enterprise-ready by shifting key concerns into the platform: security, governance, observability, and boundaries. It covers practical patterns like guardrails, CDC, service mesh, sandboxing, and MLflow tracing to move AI from demo to production safely.

video.title: Don’t burn your fingers in the heat of the AI revolution  And get an OpenClaw   by Maarten Vandeperr

talks.title: Responsibly Dimming the Lights in the Software Factory
talks.abstract: This talk shares how agentified engineering teams optimize code review for AI-generated code while avoiding cognitive debt and skill erosion. It outlines practical steps and milestones to progressively improve code quality, then safely reduce review intensity as confidence grows, gradually “dimming the lights” area by area.

video.title: Responsibly Dimming the Lights in the Software Factory  by Victor Rentea

talks.title: Specialized AI Agents: from concept to production
talks.abstract: The proposal shows how to build cheaper, specialized AI agents with minimal code using Docker Agent. It covers creating disposable agents quickly, iterating to solve real business problems, adding tools, evaluating and optimizing performance, monitoring costs, and connecting multiple agents for production collaboration.

video.title: Specialized AI Agents: from concept to production  by David Gageot

talks.title: Technical Workshop on AI-Native Tooling for Java Development
talks.abstract: This hands-on English workshop introduces AI-native Java Enterprise development using Skills, Agents, Commands, and MCP Servers. It covers prompt engineering, agent-driven workflows, and pipelines; automating lifecycle tasks; configuring framework-specific agents; extending capabilities with MCP servers; and writing effective AGENTS.md and specs for safe delegation.

talks.title: Write Java Code Like a Seasoned Hacker: 2026 Edition
talks.abstract: Hands-on session for Java developers on building secure applications in the AI era. Covers OWASP Top 10, supply chain security, SAST/SCA in CI/CD, threat modeling, monitoring and logging, secure use of AI assistants, and hardened container images, with live demos of real-world attacks and defenses.

video.title: Write Java Code Like a Seasoned Hacker: 2026 Edition  by Soroosh Khodami

talks.title: 30 minutes to build your first Vidocq app, the 100% European Sovereign Java stack with zero external dependencies
talks.abstract: Vidocq is an open-source, pure Java implementation of Jakarta EE Core Profile and MicroProfile with zero external dependencies, validated by 5,650 TCK tests. This live coding session will build a complete application from scratch, showcase its 15 modules, and promote this European sovereign Java stack.

video.title: 30 minutes to build your first Vidocq app, the 100% European Sovereign Java stack with zero external

talks.title: Analyze and Optimize Your Applications with JFR
talks.abstract: Hands-on lab on Java observability using JDK Flight Recorder (JFR). Learn to capture, manage, and analyze recordings, create custom events, and integrate JFR with Prometheus to correlate application and infrastructure behavior. Participants will gain practical skills to monitor, diagnose, and optimize Java applications.

talks.title: BootUI, the missing developer console for Spring Boot and Quarkus
talks.abstract: BooUI is a developer console for Spring Boot and Quarkus that helps you monitor users in real time, diagnose and fix issues with live view and advisor panels, and analyze memory usage for production tuning. The session includes hands-on installation and use.

video.title: BootUI, the missing developer console for Spring Boot and Quarkus  by Julien Dubois

talks.title: Building Production-Ready Agentic Systems with LangChain4j and Quarkus
talks.abstract: Hands-on lab building a production-ready agentic AI app with LangChain4j and Quarkus. Learn to integrate tools via MCP/A2A, add reusable skills, guardrails, resilience, and testing. Gain practical patterns for reliable, observable, secure, and testable agent workflows, leaving with a working enterprise-grade application.

talks.title: Solving Distributed Transactions with the Saga Pattern and Temporal
talks.abstract: This talk examines real-world challenges of implementing distributed transactions with Temporal. It covers pitfalls of classic Saga patterns, especially for synchronous workflows, failures, retries, and compensation, and explains how the architecture evolved to improve reliability, reconciliation, and consistency in production distributed systems.

video.title: Solving Distributed Transactions with the Saga Pattern and Temporal  by Andrei Sulyz

talks.title: Tap into the NVIDIA Ecosystem from Java with TornadoVM's Hybrid API
talks.abstract: TornadoVM’s Hybrid API lets Java developers combine GPU kernels written in Java with direct access to NVIDIA libraries like CUDA, cuBLAS, and cuFFT—without JNI. The session shows how to build high-performance AI/HPC apps in Java while preserving portability, productivity, and incremental acceleration within the JVM.

video.title: Tap into the NVIDIA Ecosystem from Java with TornadoVM's Hybrid API  by Thanos Stratikopoulos, Micha

talks.title: 🧰 Dev Containers: the ultimate toolbox for developers?
talks.abstract: Dev containers simplify development setup by codifying tools, frameworks, versions, and dependencies in configuration. With only Docker installed locally, developers can quickly recreate environments, avoid manual setup hassles, and manage updates consistently. This session shows how to use dev containers to build an entire development stack as code.

talks.title: AsyncAPI in action: OpenAPI for event-driven applications
talks.abstract: This session introduces AsyncAPI, the spec-first counterpart to OpenAPI for event-driven systems. Through a live demo, it generates a Spring Boot Kafka producer, consumer, DTOs, and docs from one AsyncAPI spec, showing how contract-first tooling eliminates boilerplate and keeps services and documentation aligned.

video.title: AsyncAPI in action: OpenAPI for event driven applications  by Michel Schudel

talks.title: Beyond assertEquals: Probabilistic Security and Bias Testing for Java LLM Applications
talks.abstract: This talk introduces Tiberius, a Java-native tool for LLM security and safety testing. It uses probabilistic multi-trial scans, security contracts, and statistical assertions to test adversarial attacks like prompt injections and jailbreaks, detect bias, and generate versioned JSON fixtures for regression testing.

video.title: Beyond assertEquals: Probabilistic Security and Bias Testing for Java LLM Applications  by Iryna Doh

talks.title: From Laptop to Lakehouse: Analytical SQL with DuckDB
talks.abstract: DuckDB is a fast, open-source in-process analytical SQL engine with no server or dependencies. This session demos its scale from laptop analytics on CSV/JSON/Parquet to embedded Java apps, S3 queries, and lakehouse use with DuckLake and Quack, aimed at developers and engineers needing simple data analysis.

video.title: From Laptop to Lakehouse: Analytical SQL with DuckDB  by Oliver Geisser

talks.title: The Java Story | The Official Documentary
talks.abstract: A documentary tracing 31 years of Java’s evolution—from Sun Microsystems to OpenJDK and Jakarta EE—through the voices of its creators and community. It highlights innovation, reinvention, and the collective effort that kept Java alive as one of the world’s most influential software platforms.

talks.title: The Magic of OpenTelemetry: Rewriting Your App in Production
talks.abstract: This talk explains how the OpenTelemetry Java agent works inside the JVM: class loading interception, runtime bytecode rewriting, and ByteBuddy-based instrumentation of frameworks like Spring, JDBC, and gRPC. It also covers production impacts such as latency, allocations, conflicts, and debugging techniques.

video.title: The Magic of OpenTelemetry: Rewriting Your App in Production   by Bruce Bujon

talks.title: Do We Need a Build Language? Java Builds Java
talks.abstract: Jenesis is a proof-of-concept Java build tool embedded as source code, making builds easier to run, modify, and understand without external setup. It also aims to improve supply-chain security, reproducibility, and maintainability by separating build logic from dependencies and using the Java module system.

video.title: Do We Need a Build Language? Java Builds Java  by Rafael Winterhalter

talks.title: Exquisite Evals for Skills & MCPs
talks.abstract: The speaker built the javadocs.dev MCP server to give Java, Kotlin, and Scala agents efficient library documentation access. They created a custom eval framework showing it is up to 5x more token-efficient and more accurate than base models or web search. The session shares best practices for effective evals.

video.title: Exquisite Evals for Skills & MCPs  by Christian Tzolov, James Ward

talks.title: Java Script (No, Not That One): Modern Automation with Java
talks.abstract: The talk shows how modern Java has become practical for scripting and automation, thanks to shebang support, single-file execution, and instance main methods. It also covers JBang for dependency management and advanced use cases, with live demos demonstrating fast, maintainable Java scripts.

video.title: Java Script No, Not That One: Modern Automation with Java  by Loïc Magnette

talks.title: The Importance of HITL to Avoid Chaos and EU Regulations for AI
talks.abstract: The talk explains Human-in-the-Loop design for AI coding agents in enterprise workflows, covering approval gates, audit trails, compliance with the EU AI Act, and failure risks in microservices. It offers practical patterns for adding human checkpoints to CI/CD without sacrificing speed or control.

video.title: The Importance of HITL to Avoid Chaos and EU Regulations for AI  by Juan Antonio Breña 🇪🇸🇪🇺

talks.title: Quarkus Community BOF
talks.abstract: Quarkus is a fast-growing Java framework with 800+ extensions and 1,000+ contributors, now under the CommonHaus Foundation. Meet core team and contributors at Devoxx to discuss the ecosystem, share ideas, and ask anything—especially about Quarkus, community involvement, and its work on Agentic AI.

talks.title: Who will build software after AI?
talks.abstract: An open discussion on how AI-assisted development affects children’s coding education, including whether kids should still learn to code, which skills matter most, and how to make technology engaging and accessible. The session explores the future of Devoxx4Kids, robotics, and nurturing the next generation of makers.

talks.title: Keynote overflow room
talks.abstract: The keynote overflow room. The keynote overflow room. The keynote overflow room. The keynote overflow room.

talks.title: Welcome to Devoxx
talks.abstract: The welcome opening keynote for Devoxx Belgium 2026 by the founder of Devoxx giving a general update on the conference.

video.title: Welcome to Devoxx Belgium 2026 by Stephan Janssen

talks.title: From Brainless to Brilliant — Giving an Open-Source Robot a Mind of Its Own
talks.abstract: A hobbyist built AURA, a personal “brain” for an open robot platform, using only a laptop. It recognizes household members, keeps learned and told information separate, and seeks permission before committing code. The project demonstrates how accessible robotics and AI now are.

video.title: From Brainless to Brilliant — Giving an Open Source Robot a Mind of Its Own  by Jan Van Wassenhove

talks.title: Half of a billion Idle GPUs: The Case for On-Device AI
talks.abstract: This keynote argues that Apple Silicon devices form a massive, underused AI compute fleet. Drawing on the MLX ecosystem, it shows how on-device inference can handle frontier models through advanced optimization, and why privacy, latency, cost, and sovereignty will shift more AI workloads from cloud to device.

video.title: Half of a billion Idle GPUs: The Case for On Device AI  by Prince Canuma

talks.title: A Fleet of AI Agents, Each in Its Own Sandbox: Inside Docker's Agentic Platform
talks.abstract: Docker’s Agentic Platform enables AI agents to autonomously read issues, code, test, and prepare pull requests in isolated sandboxes with secure identities. The talk covers orchestrated specialist agents, parallel workflows, and key production lessons on cost, hallucinations, human oversight, safety, and observability.

video.title: A Fleet of AI Agents, Each in Its Own Sandbox: Inside Docker's Agentic Platform  by Jean Laurent de

talks.title: The Year of the Runtime
talks.abstract: AI coding agents reduce the importance of language syntax, making runtime performance and operability more critical. Java’s JVM and standard library are a strong fit: newer JDKs continually improve speed, observability, garbage collection, and usability without changing the programming model, with major innovations underway in Valhalla, Leyden, and Lilliput.

video.title: The Year of the Runtime  by Ron Pressler

talks.title: Agentic Engineering Reconversion
talks.abstract: This keynote examines the evolving role of software engineers amid AI-driven transformation. Drawing on lessons from hundreds of developers worldwide, it explores balancing personal life, uncertainty, and excitement; accelerating AI-focused reskilling; and adapting effectively to the profession’s rapidly changing future.

video.title: Agentic Engineering Reconversion  by Victor Rentea

talks.title: Build the Builder: A Java Coding Agent in Your IDE with ACP
talks.abstract: This session shows how to build a production-ready coding agent in Java/Kotlin, connect it to IntelliJ via ACP, and orchestrate external agents like Codex, Claude, and Gemini. It covers reasoning loops, tools, guardrails, IDE context, and coordinated multi-agent workflows for real software engineering tasks.

video.title: Build the Builder: A Java Coding Agent in Your IDE with ACP  by Vadim Briliantov

talks.title: Emergent DevEx: The Good, the Bad, and the Legacy
talks.abstract: This talk explores how developer experience deteriorates as organizations scale, creating bureaucratic friction and outdated internal tools. It argues that copying DevEx models from companies like Google or Netflix is misguided, and offers strategies for engineers to shape and resist tool-driven bureaucracy.

video.title: Emergent DevEx: The Good, the Bad, and the Legacy  by Makan Sepehrifar, Soroosh Khodami

talks.title: Fun with Flags: How OpenFeature Solves Your Feature Flag Headaches
talks.abstract: Feature flags improve agile software delivery, but complexity grows with targeting, multi-language support, vendor lock-in, and cleanup. This talk explores common feature flag pitfalls and shows how OpenFeature’s vendor-agnostic SDKs and tools simplify flag management and make the process easier.

video.title: Fun with Flags: How OpenFeature Solves Your Feature Flag Headaches  by Simon Schrottner

talks.title: I Hired a Real Robot as My Junior Dev — and Now My Kids Don't Want to Learn Java Anymore
talks.abstract: A humorous talk on how AI agents and desktop robots may commoditize coding while increasing the value of architecture, systems thinking, and product judgment. It explores a shift from typing code to directing agents in natural language, asking whether we’re training the last generation of developers.

video.title: I Hired a Real Robot as My Junior Dev — and Now My Kids Don't Want to Learn Java Anymore  by Jan Van

talks.title: MCP 2.0 - Stateless, New Auth (CIMD), and Exciting Extensions
talks.abstract: The session reviews recent MCP spec and implementation changes and their impact on server developers. It covers stateless transport, new CIMD authentication, and extensions like MCP Apps, Tasks, and Skills. Code examples and demos show how to build servers using the latest MCP features and approaches.

video.title: MCP 2 0   Stateless, New Auth CIMD, and Exciting Extensions  by James Ward

talks.title: Post-Quantum Today: How Your Passwords Will Be Safe in a Quantum Future
talks.abstract: This talk explains RSA encryption, how Shor’s algorithm could break it, the current state of quantum hardware, and why post-quantum cryptography matters now. It also introduces lattice-based quantum-safe encryption and current adoption progress, helping audiences understand future cryptography and “harvest now, decrypt later” risks.

video.title: Post Quantum Today: How Your Passwords Will Be Safe in a Quantum Future  by Julian Burr

talks.title: Structured Concurrency Looms
talks.abstract: Structured Concurrency in Project Loom builds on virtual threads to simplify concurrent programming by treating related tasks as one unit. It improves cancellation, error handling, and observability, and makes code easier to understand and debug. The session covers its design, usage, evolution, and future lower-level API work.

video.title: Structured Concurrency Looms  by Alan Bateman, Viktor Klang

talks.title: Wrap, Reshape, or Redesign: Retrofitting Your APIs for a World of Agents
talks.abstract: The talk explores how to adapt human-designed APIs for LLM agents, which interpret instructions literally and need explicit boundaries. It presents a practical framework for retrofitting APIs into agent-ready tools, with real examples, tradeoffs, and cases where redesign improves both agent and human usability.

video.title: Wrap, Reshape, or Redesign: Retrofitting Your APIs for a World of Agents  by Horacio Gonzalez Zaal 1

talks.title: AI Doesn’t Click Buttons: Building APIs for the Agentic Age
talks.abstract: This session explains how to design AI-first APIs for copilots and autonomous agents. It covers contract-first design, typed schemas, explainable errors, machine-readable actions, security, observability, OpenAPI, Java records, and legacy migration strategies, helping developers evolve existing APIs without rewriting applications.

video.title: AI Doesn’t Click Buttons :APIs for the Agentic Age  by Kim Lauwers

talks.title: Engineering for the Long Haul: Operating Open Source at Scale
talks.abstract: The presentation explains how enterprises can securely and compliantly manage open-source software over time despite short lifecycles and upgrade demands. It highlights TuxCare solutions—rebootless patching, end-of-life security updates, low-noise vulnerability scanning, and enterprise support—to extend software life and reduce risk.

video.title: Engineering for the Long Haul: Operating Open Source at Scale  by Sven Sellen

talks.title: Eval Driven Development: Why you need it to make your Agentic Application survive Production
talks.abstract: Eval-Driven Development (EDD) adapts test-driven development to agentic AI systems, helping manage hallucinations, drift, and workflow surprises. This talk shows how to build reliable agents with layered evals, golden datasets, rubrics, trace signals, and regression gates, using JVM AI frameworks like Spring AI, LangChain4J, and Koog.

video.title: Eval Driven Development: Why you need it to make your Agentic Application survive Production  by  Ur

talks.title: From User Prompt to JPA Query: Comparing Tool Calling, Structured Output & Hybrid Approach
talks.abstract: The project compares three LLM approaches for natural-language database filtering in a Java Spring AI/Vaadin app: function calling, structured output, and a hybrid method. Tested with local Ollama models, it evaluates reliability, speed, cost, and limitations for handling complex filter requests.

video.title: From User Prompt to JPA Query: Comparing Tool Calling, Structured Output & Hybrid Approach  by Sebas

talks.title: Let's dance! – Teaching your robot some moves with reinforcement learning
talks.abstract: A humorous talk on training a humanoid robot to walk and dance using reinforcement learning in simulation. It introduces RL basics, NVIDIA Isaac Sim, Unitree RL Lab, motion retargeting from video, and imitation learning, ending with a live dancing performance by the robot.

video.title: Let's dance! – Teaching your robot some moves with reinforcement learning  by Thomas Endres, Martin

talks.title: Life in the Ivory Tower: Confessions of a Former Developer Who Turned Into an Architect
talks.abstract: A humorous talk about becoming an enterprise architect and bridging the gap between hands-on development and corporate IT decision-making. It explores the psychology behind technical choices, staying technically current while moving up, and fostering collaboration between developers and architects.

video.title: Life in the Ivory Tower   Confessions of a Former Developer Who Turned Into an Architect by Robin cu

talks.title: Mission Possible: The 45-Minute Path to Bullet-Proof Java Container Images
talks.abstract: A lunch session on hardening Java container images by reducing CVE noise and operational risk. It covers choosing minimal base images, shrinking privileges, pinning versions, signing and SBOMs, using CVSS-based scanning, and automating updates with Dependabot/Renovate, with practical Dockerfile guidance and verification steps.

video.title: Mission Possible: The 45 Minute Path to Bullet Proof Java Container Images  by Pasha Finkelshtein

talks.title: Safety, speed, and governance in the agentic era
talks.abstract: The session explores Docker Sandboxes as a secure local isolation layer for AI agents, limiting filesystem and credential access. It also addresses how agents can still leak data, and proposes a multi-layered approach combining sandboxing, tool governance, and policy controls for safer, trustworthy agent execution.

video.title: Safety, speed, and governance in the agentic era  by Oleg Šelajev

talks.title: A Year of Agentic AI Evolution: Lessons Learned Building Production-grade Agentic Systems
talks.abstract: LangChain4j’s agentic framework has evolved from fixed patterns to flexible orchestration, letting developers compose strategies for different use cases. The session covers new built-in patterns, their trade-offs, and production features like tracing, state persistence, failure recovery, and human-in-the-loop pauses.

video.title: A Year of Agentic AI Evolution by Mario Fusco & Kevin Dubois

talks.title: Deterministic by Design - Achieving Reproducible Builds with Maven
talks.abstract: This session shows how Apache Maven can make builds reproducible by producing identical artifacts from identical inputs. It explains how to diagnose non-determinism, use Maven’s verification tools, and improve traceability and compliance in software delivery pipelines increasingly scrutinized by auditors and regulators.

video.title: Deterministic by Design   Achieving Reproducible Builds with Maven  by Maarten Mulders

talks.title: G1, ZGC, Shenandoah, ... with all these GCs in Java, which one do I choose?
talks.abstract: This talk explains why Java has multiple garbage collectors, what ZGC, Shenandoah, and others do, and their strengths and weaknesses. It traces GC history, compares alternatives, and shows when to use each one for the right project, application, or environment.

talks.title: Harness Engineering: Building the System Around Your AI Coding Agent
talks.abstract: AI coding agents are fundamentally simple: prompt a model, execute tool calls, feed results back, and repeat. This talk builds such an engine in Java, then iteratively adds context, constraints, and feedback to show how real tools improve reliability, safety, and understanding of their limits.

video.title: Harness Engineering: Building the System Around Your AI Coding Agent   by JI Darwish

talks.title: Java, Raspberry Pi, and the Art of Overengineering Everyday Life
talks.abstract: Java developers can build practical Raspberry Pi home automation without leaving their tools. This talk shows two real projects—a BBQ smoker controller and a jetty server for photos, water levels, and fishing alerts—covering hardware access, deployment, reliable services, mobile UIs, and secure remote control.

video.title: java raspberry Pi and the art of by Matti Tahvonen

talks.title: Run Frontier Open Models on consumer hardware
talks.abstract: A deep dive into fast, production-grade on-device inference on Macs using the MLX ecosystem. Covers unified memory, continuous batching, KV-cache compression, speculative decoding, and model porting pitfalls, with real benchmark results and engineering tradeoffs for balancing accuracy, latency, and memory on consumer hardware.

video.title: Run Frontier Open Models on consumer hardware  by Prince Canuma

talks.title: The pizza party of the future 🍕 software teams and product value in the age of coding agents
talks.abstract: AI is reshaping software teams, creating new bottlenecks around value and trust. The talk explores how developer roles, team structures, and responsibilities may evolve—from cross-functional teams to AI-assisted models—drawing on past agile critiques to imagine a more value-driven future of human-agent collaboration.

video.title: The pizza party of the future 🍕 by Katie Clark and Simon Rohrer

talks.title: What rules the virtual? How our systems obey physical laws.
talks.abstract: This proposal explores the physical foundations of information and computation, asking how data is stored, moved, and erased in the real world. It examines energy, speed, and disappearance of information, then extends into quantum effects and how stable states emerge beneath digital abstractions.

video.title: What rules the virtual? How our systems obey physical laws   by Marianne Hoornenborg

talks.title: 0 to 350 Engineers on Claude Code: What Could Go Wrong?
talks.abstract: AI coding agents are transforming software development, enabling non-developers to build features and teams to work end-to-end. The talk explores real-world adoption, risks like large uncontrolled changes, cost management, and how developers and organizations must adapt to prompting, agents, skills, and CI/CD.

video.title: 0 to 350 Engineers on Claude Code: What Could Go Wrong?  by Nicolas Martignole

talks.title: Bootiful Spring Boot 4
talks.abstract: Explore Spring Boot 4.x with Java 25+, covering scalable, modular, secure, and intelligent applications. Learn about the Spring ecosystem, AI integration, seamless data access, and production optimizations including virtual threads, Project Leyden, GraalVM, and more for building faster, more efficient systems.

video.title: Bootiful Spring Boot 4  by Josh Long

talks.title: CRAcking Compliance - The EU Cyber Resilience Act
talks.abstract: The talk explains the EU Cyber Resilience Act, its impact, and new compliance requirements. It covers SBOM generation for Java, .NET, and JavaScript projects, CI integration, vulnerability management with Dependabot/Renovate, and reducing risk through automated dependency updates and distroless images.

video.title: CRAcking Compliance   The EU Cyber Resilience Act  by Christian Schabetsberger

talks.title: How to survive and thrive as a dev (team) in the exponential age of AI. Real-world AI adoption, smarter ways of working, and lessons from the front lines
talks.abstract: Sander Hoogendoorn shares a practical, no-hype view of AI at iBOOD: how it’s reshaping product architecture, engineering, and team culture. He covers real risks like lock-in and fragile dependencies, and explains why autonomous microteams, experimentation, and adaptability replace traditional processes in the AI era.

video.title: How to survive and thrive as a dev team in the exponential age of AI  Real world AI adoption, smarte

talks.title: Integration patterns for distributed systems
talks.abstract: The session explains distributed-systems challenges in modern interconnected applications—such as retries, idempotence, ordering, and failures—and the design trade-offs and patterns used to manage them. It targets architects, developers, and executives, and offers guidance for modernizing legacy systems into loosely coupled, flexible, scalable architectures.

video.title: Integration patterns for distributed systems  by Dirk Fröhner, Sabarish Sekar

talks.title: Pragmatic multi-cloud architecture: designing for resilience and portability beyond the hype
talks.abstract: This session explores designing a real-world multi-cloud platform, weighing the benefits of using multiple providers against challenges like latency, fragmented data, incompatible APIs, security, and SLA risks. It covers bounded contexts, production hurdles, API design, best practices, and pragmatic risk analysis to guide coherent architecture decisions.

video.title: Pragmatic multi cloud architecture: designing for resilience and portability beyond the hype   by Al

talks.title: Teaching an Old Handle New Tricks: From Core Reflection to FFM
talks.abstract: The talk explains how Java reflection is inefficient, and how method handles and var handles create reusable, typed capabilities that better match JVM linkage. It also shows how this design supports newer APIs like Foreign Function & Memory and serialization, illustrating resilient platform design.

video.title: Teaching an Old Handle New Tricks: From Core Reflection to FFM  by Maurizio Cimadamore, Viktor Klang

talks.title: Why Documentation Won’t Write Itself—and AI Won’t Save You
talks.abstract: The talk argues that AI won’t solve poor documentation. It presents practical principles for keeping docs close to code, separating architecture/API/code-level documentation, and preventing decay. Key takeaway: missing context remains missing unless teams make deliberate documentation decisions first.

video.title: Why Documentation Won’t Write Itself—and AI Won’t Save You  by Christian Heitzmann

talks.title: AI Made Building Cheap. Now Decisions Are the Bottleneck.
talks.abstract: AI is making software delivery faster, shifting the main bottleneck from execution to decision-making. This talk shows how AI can improve discovery, architecture, and delivery conversations, turning discussions into maps, diagrams, risks, and options to expose complexity, align stakeholders, and make better decisions.

video.title: AI Made Building Cheap  Now Decisions Are the Bottleneck   by Dave Sammut, João Rosa

talks.title: Architecture Observability and Guardrails
talks.abstract: Talk on preventing “AI slop” by enforcing code quality in AI-generated codebases. It covers agent design feedback loops and ways to preserve human review bandwidth, using C4 models, PlantUML, captured sequence diagrams, complexity visualizations, and efficient testing practices.

video.title: Architecture Observability and Guardrails  by Victor Rentea

talks.title: Big Runtimes Make Efficient Programs
talks.abstract: Large runtimes, like the JVM, can improve both convenience and performance by enabling JIT compilation and garbage collection. This challenges the idea that smaller runtimes and more compile-time decisions are always faster, showing the real tradeoffs are more complex.

video.title: Big Runtimes Make Efficient Programs  by Ron Pressler

talks.title: Building LLM Inference Engines in Java with TornadoVM and the NVIDIA Ecosystem
talks.abstract: The session shows how Java can run GPU-accelerated local LLMs natively with TornadoVM, using NVIDIA libraries without JNI. It covers GPULlama3.java, quantized inference, Quarkus and LangChain4J integration, and how TornadoVM plus Project Babylon/Panama position Java as a strong AI and HPC platform.

video.title: Building LLM Inference Engines in Java with TornadoVM and the NVIDIA Ecosystem  by Thanos Stratikopo

talks.title: Building an Agent Ready Platform
talks.abstract: This session explains how to move AI agents from demo to production using platform engineering: secure model access, agent identity, inherited guardrails, and observability for actions and cost. It shows what developers should ask for from platform teams, and what platform teams should build first.

video.title: Building an Agent Ready Platform  by Timo Salm

talks.title: Consistency Patterns in Event-Driven Architecture
talks.abstract: This talk explains how to avoid inconsistencies in distributed systems caused by dual writes and failed transactions. It covers Outbox/Inbox patterns, idempotent consumers, and Saga orchestration/choreography, showing when to use each and the trade-offs involved with eventual consistency.

video.title: Consistency Patterns in Event Driven Architecture  by Emanuel Trandafir

talks.title: GraalVM Next: Layers, Crema, and WebAssembly in Action
talks.abstract: The session explores three GraalVM Native Image projects: Native Image Layers for shared code and memory, Project Crema for dynamic class loading at runtime, and Web Image for compiling JVM apps to WebAssembly for browsers. Together, they expand packaging, runtime behavior, and deployment targets.

video.title: GraalVM Next: Layers, Crema, and WebAssembly in Action  by Alina Yurenko

talks.title: Surviving the "AI Slopageddon": How AI shakes the foundations of Open Source
talks.abstract: Vibe Coding boosts productivity but overwhelms open-source maintainers with low-quality AI-generated pull requests, hallucinated bug reports, and autonomous agents. This talk examines AI’s existential threat to open source and proposes defensive strategies such as stricter access, restructuring workflows, and machine-adapted governance.

video.title: Surviving the "AI Slopageddon": How AI shakes the foundations of Open Source  by Raphael Semeteys

talks.title: A Deserter Returns: What the Java community helped me rediscover
talks.abstract: A developer explains leaving Java for Python, then rediscovering Java through picocli, Quarkus, and TamboUI. The talk explores Java’s modern CLI, fast native apps, and terminal UIs, showing how community and new tooling made Java relevant again.

talks.title: Beyond encryption at rest: computing on encrypted data
talks.abstract: This talk explains Homomorphic Encryption, which enables computation on encrypted data without decryption. It covers core concepts, modern Fully Homomorphic Encryption, practical applications in confidential AI, healthcare, and finance, and current limitations such as performance, ciphertext size, and implementation complexity.

video.title: Beyond encryption at rest: computing on encrypted data  by Andrea Iacono

talks.title: Create your own AI Agents without code
talks.abstract: Docker Agent is an open-source, no-code platform for creating specialized AI agents quickly and affordably. It supports testing, benchmarking, optimization, and collaborative multi-agent workflows, while working with any LLM provider.

video.title: Create your own AI Agents without code  by David Gageot

talks.title: Kubernetes for Developers
talks.abstract: Kubernetes for developers: what you need to know, without becoming a Kubernetes expert.

video.title: Kubernetes for Developers  by Alain Regnier

talks.title: No Country For Old APIs. Wrapping legacy Java services as MCP tools without rewriting them.
talks.abstract: A demo-driven session on connecting AI agents to legacy Java, REST, and SOAP enterprise systems using MCP, Spring AI, and GraphQL. It tackles real brownfield challenges—auth, tool sprawl, oversized responses, and unsafe retries—and offers reusable patterns for secure, practical integration.

video.title: No Country For Old APIs  Wrapping legacy Java services as MCP tools without rewriting them   by Žel

talks.title: Quarkus Meets Leyden at the JVM Performance Edge
talks.abstract: This talk shares hands-on Quarkus experiments with Project Leyden, exploring how Leyden’s JVM startup and warm-up improvements interact with Quarkus’ build-time optimizations. It highlights what works, current limitations, performance findings, broken assumptions, and design changes needed to combine both approaches effectively.

video.title: Quarkus Meets Leyden at the JVM Performance Edge  by Georgios Andrianakis, Ana Maria Mihalceanu

talks.title: When benchmarks go bad - what we learned from measuring performance wrong
talks.abstract: This talk explores common performance measurement mistakes, cognitive biases, and misleading intuitions. Franz and Holly explain why performance testing matters, how it can go wrong, and offer practical guidance for improving application performance, including test system setup, load generators, and the USE method.

video.title: When benchmarks go bad   what we learned from measuring performance wrong  by Francesco Nigro, Holly

talks.title: rm -rf self-doubt: Debugging Impostor Syndrome for Developers
talks.abstract: This session explains the neuroscience behind imposter syndrome in software teams and offers practical strategies to manage self-doubt, respond better to feedback, and grow through discomfort. Attendees will gain immediately usable tools for code reviews, design discussions, and stepping into larger roles.

video.title: rm  rf self doubt: Debugging Impostor Syndrome for Developers  by Vincent Mayers

talks.title: Getting started with speaking: Your first conference talk
talks.abstract: This session, led by experienced speakers, offers practical guidance on starting technical speaking: choosing topics, writing proposals, preparing talks, and delivering effectively. It shares lessons learned, successes, failures, and key takeaways to help attendees begin their own speaking journey.

talks.title: GraalVM Community BOF
talks.abstract: Join GraalVM core members for updates on Crema, enabling dynamic class loading in Native Image, and news across GraalOS, GraalPy, GraalWasm, Micronaut, and the broader ecosystem. This community BOF invites questions, feedback, and ideas to help shape GraalVM’s future.

talks.title: 223 Pull Requests in 11 Days: The Recipe for Building Real Software with AI Agents
talks.abstract: An AI-agent workflow enabled building an 83,000-line Spring Boot developer UI in 11 days instead of 6.5–8.5 months. The talk explains how to orchestrate multiple agents with specs, tests, and parallel overnight builds to achieve major productivity gains while delivering a new developer console.

video.title: 223 Pull Requests in 11 Days: The Recipe for Building Real Software with AI Agents  by Julien Dubois

talks.title: AI without spaghetti: Clean architecture in the age of AI
talks.abstract: A case study of a chatbot that evolves into a platform, showing how “just ship it” AI code becomes brittle. The session demonstrates refactoring to Clean Architecture, separating domain, application, and infrastructure so models, prompts, and pipelines can change safely and scale.

video.title: AI without spaghetti: Clean architecture in these of AI  by Maarten Vandeperre en Lutske van der Mee

talks.title: From vibe coding to harness engineering: modernizing a regulated environment with AI
talks.abstract: AI-enabled migration of a banking mainframe to the cloud required a shift from “vibe coding” to “harness engineering.” The talk shows how to control AI-generated code in regulated environments through spec-driven development, evolutionary pipelines, and continuous validation, balancing agility, safety, and changing security rules.

video.title: From vibe coding to harness engineering: modernizing a regulated environment with AI by Anyul Rivas

talks.title: Java on Kubernetes Without Container Images: The WebAssembly Way
talks.abstract: The talk shows how KWasm-style runtime delegation can let Java apps run on Kubernetes without container images. It explains containerd internals, custom shims, node provisioners, and CRDs, then demonstrates Brewlet.sh, a new open-source project that deploys a Spring Boot JAR directly as an OCI artifact.

video.title: Java on Kubernetes Without Container Images: The WebAssembly Way By Bruno Borges

talks.title: Project Detroit: From Foreign Libraries to Foreign Language Runtimes
talks.abstract: Project Detroit uses Java’s Foreign Function & Memory API to embed native runtimes like V8 and CPython directly into Java applications. It replaces custom reimplementations like Nashorn with standard runtimes, exploring challenges such as garbage collection coordination and virtual thread pinning.

video.title: Project Detroit: From Foreign Libraries to Foreign Language Runtimes  by Maurizio Cimadamore

talks.title: Rewriting the rules: How AI transforms engineering and inspiring young minds
talks.abstract: This talk shows how AI drives innovation in regulated banking, improving developer productivity through agentic automation, prompt libraries and Copilot. It also highlights social impact via Devoxx4Kids, where engineers built playful coding and cybersecurity learning platforms for children, inspiring the next generation.

video.title: How AI transforms engineering and inspiring young minds – Ayoub Hammou Ahabchane & Kamel Zaraoui

talks.title: Snake in 10 Lines: Learning More by Coding Less
talks.abstract: A live-coding talk recreates Snake in 10 lines of JDK-only code, overcoming input and design challenges to distill the game’s essence. The project demonstrates how extreme conciseness fosters creativity, deeper understanding, and transferable problem-solving techniques.

video.title: Snake in 10 Lines: Learning More by Coding Less  by Guus de Wit

talks.title: Toxic Flows in MCP Servers and Skills: What Your Agent Blindly Trusts
talks.abstract: This talk introduces “toxic flows” in AI agent stacks: trust paths through MCP servers and Skills that can leak context, manipulate decisions, and trigger unintended actions. It shows how trust failures arise, parallels familiar software risks, and offers a framework for identifying boundaries and hardening agent integrations.

video.title: Toxic Flows in MCP Servers and Skills: What Your Agent Blindly Trusts by Brian Vermeer

talks.title: Agents With Seatbelts: Practical Ways to Keep AI Code Gen Under Control
talks.abstract: This session shares best practices for MCP setups and AI agents in development workflows, focusing on quality, security, and avoiding unintended actions. It compares LLM code-generation stability and consistency, and addresses how to measure AI-driven improvement, helping teams build reliable, productive, and safe AI workflows.

talks.title: Coder, Coach, Catalyst - using questions to make people grow
talks.abstract: This talk teaches technologists basic coaching skills—listening, asking better questions, and using informal to formal coaching—to help others solve their own problems, foster growth, and reduce the burden of constantly taking on teammates’ issues.

video.title: Coder, Coach, Catalyst   using questions to make people grow  by Martin Mazur

talks.title: Dream Machines & Walled Gardens
talks.abstract: The talk profiles Ted Nelson and his 1974 manifesto *Computer Lib/Dream Machines*, which envisioned computers as tools for freedom, creativity, and open hypertext. It asks how the internet might differ today if Nelson’s user-centered, decentralized vision had prevailed over Big Tech’s closed, algorithmic systems.

video.title: Dream Machines & Walled Gardens  by Anders Norås

talks.title: Hey Belfius! Meet our new bank AI assistant—and discover how we’re building and securing AI across Belfius.
talks.abstract: Belfius is reimagining everyday banking with Hey Belfius, an AI personal assistant that answers questions, anticipates needs and enables proactive actions. The proposal explores building trusted AI experiences while ensuring security, covering AI-driven security techniques, secure development practices, and protection against malicious AI use.

video.title: Hey Belfius! Meet our new bank AI assistant—and discover how we’re building and securing AI across B

talks.title: High-Performance Java-Native AI with CUDA and the Vector API
talks.abstract: This session shows how modern Java, using the Foreign Function & Memory API and Vector API, can run high-performance AI natively on CPUs and GPUs without JNI or Python. It includes Deep Netts CUDA integration, SIMD acceleration, and a fraud detection use case.

video.title: High Performance Java Native AI with CUDA and the Vector API  by Zoran Sevarac

talks.title: How to Architect Green Software
talks.abstract: The session examines sustainability trade-offs in architecture decisions, balancing energy use and carbon footprint against maintainability, portability, availability, and performance. It offers practical techniques to reduce emissions and costs, and provides a catalog of trade-offs to apply in future projects.

video.title: How to Architect Green Software by Ioannis Kolaxis

talks.title: Reflect, Transform, Accelerate: Bringing GPU Computing to Java
talks.abstract: The talk presents HAT, a toolkit using Java Code Reflection to accelerate Java workloads on GPUs through reflection, transformation, and offloading to OpenCL or CUDA. It includes tensor-core and matrix-multiplication examples, plus performance profiling and tuning with NVIDIA Nsight Compute and Nsight Systems.

video.title: Reflect, Transform, Accelerate: Bringing GPU Computing to Java By Juan Fumero

talks.title: When ORM Becomes OMG: Performance Pitfalls in JPA and Friends
talks.abstract: This talk examines common JPA performance pitfalls, from unexpected data loading and transaction issues to connection mismanagement. Using a sample app, it shows how libraries and tooling can reveal real-world ORM problems and help prevent slowdowns in Spring Data JPA applications.

video.title: When ORM Becomes OMG: Performance Pitfalls in JPA and Friends  by Jos Roseboom

talks.title: Making sense of vector databases
talks.abstract: This talk explains vector databases, covering vectors, embeddings, indexing algorithms, and similarity metrics. It demonstrates a simple in-memory vector database using Java’s Vector API and integrates with other vector databases via Spring AI, progressing from basic use cases to advanced applications.

video.title: Making sense of vector databases  by Balkrishna Rawool

talks.title: Quixotic: Pure Java Inference at Native Speed
talks.abstract: Quixotic brings AI to Java by running models in-process as pure Java, with no Python, ONNX, or native dependencies. It keeps sensitive data inside the JVM, compiles models into fast native binaries, and enables secure, portable AI for regulated industries.

video.title: Quixotic: Pure Java Inference at Native Speed  by Alfonso² Peterssen

talks.title: SIMD for Java: how Elasticsearch already benefits from the Panama Vector API
talks.abstract: This talk explains how Elasticsearch uses Java’s Panama Vector API to accelerate vector search and analytical queries with SIMD instructions. It shows how Lucene and Elasticsearch enable runtime SIMD safely, despite the API being incubating, and discusses implications for high-performance Java computing.

video.title: SIMD for Java: how Elasticsearch already benefits from the Panama Vector API  by Piotr Przybyl

talks.title: Say Goodbye to LLM API keys with Workload Identity Federation
talks.abstract: The session explains why API keys are unsafe for production LLM access and how Workload Identity Federation replaces them with short-lived tokens. It covers SPIFFE and Kubernetes service tokens as workload identities, then demonstrates a Quarkus LangChain4j app using SPIFFE-issued JWTs with Anthropic WIF.

video.title: Say Goodbye to LLM API keys with Workload Identity Federation  by Siarhei Biarozkin

talks.title: State of Agentic Coding
talks.abstract: This session reviews recent advances in agentic coding, from MCP to skills, and explores ways to build trust in AI coding agents. It includes live demos of practical development workflows and an overview of the Google Antigravity ecosystem.

video.title: State of Agentic Coding  by Daniela Petruzalek

talks.title: Taming Microservice Overload: Our Journey to Modular Monoliths
talks.abstract: At the Port of Rotterdam, an overgrown microservices architecture created operational complexity and fragmented ownership. This talk shows how Domain-Driven Design and Spring Modulith were used to consolidate services into modular monoliths, preserving domain boundaries while improving maintainability, clarity, and team ownership.

video.title: Taming Microservice Overload: Our Journey to Modular Monoliths  by Mario Klaver

talks.title: The Rise of Agent Enablement: Coding Agents Don't Scale Themselves. Neither Do Your Teams.
talks.abstract: The talk argues that “dark factory” readiness is organizational, not technical. Using Conway’s Law, it outlines four enablement layers: agent, team, platform, and organization. It targets engineering leaders scaling agentic coding beyond tools, focusing on roles, rituals, infrastructure, ROI, and knowledge capture.

video.title: The Rise of Agent Enablement: Coding Agents Don't Scale Themselves  Neither Do Your Teams  by Patric

talks.title: The Yearly Java Performance Update for 2026
talks.abstract: This talk surveys recent Java performance improvements across the JDK—libraries, HotSpot, JIT, and GC—showing how they boost startup, memory use, throughput, and virtual-thread scalability. It explains what upgrades deliver automatically, what needs tuning, and how engineers measure real-world impact.

video.title: The Yearly Java Performance Update for 2026 by Per Ake Minborg

talks.title: "You May Now Optimize the Wedding": Optimizing the Seating, Bachelor Party, and Honeymoon with Constraint AI
talks.abstract: This talk shows how to automate complex planning problems using constraint optimization. Using wedding scenarios like seating charts, pub crawls, and honeymoon itineraries, it demonstrates how Timefold solves scheduling, routing, and planning challenges with real code and constraints, turning “could I automate this?” into working optimization solutions.

video.title: "You May Now Optimize the Wedding": Optimizing the Seating, Bachelor Party, and Honeymoon with Const

talks.title: Agents Shouldn't Control Control Flow
talks.abstract: A deterministic compiler turns an enterprise context graph into governed agent workflows in Java, with control flow treated as a build artifact. The LLM only writes summaries, while code passes through Git, CI, tests, and human review, reducing hallucination risk and enabling policy-controlled changes.

video.title: Agents Shouldn't Control Control Flow by Jeremy Adams

talks.title: Engineering Lessons from Working on Software Older Than Me
talks.abstract: A session on engineering lessons from maintaining and scaling legacy PDF technology, covering compatibility, performance, security, testing, and interoperability. It shows how mature systems teach resilient software design and highlights the invisible challenges behind reliable user experiences.

video.title: Engineering Lessons from Working on Software Older Than Me  by Guust Ysebie

talks.title: Green Maven builds: sustainable CI in practice
talks.abstract: This session shows practical ways to make Maven builds greener and faster by improving CI pipelines. Using GitLab CI and GitHub Actions examples, it demonstrates techniques to reduce energy use, save machine resources, and cut build time.

video.title: Green Maven builds: sustainable CI in practice by Jan Boonen

talks.title: Is the IDE dead ?
talks.abstract: This session explores how AI is reshaping developer tools, questioning the future of traditional IDEs versus terminal-based workflows. It examines what engineers need in 2026, how AI agents are becoming power users, and what these shifts mean for tool builders and software engineers.

video.title: Is the IDE dead ?  by Martin Lippert

talks.title: Keeping Spring Applications Secure in the Age of AI
talks.abstract: AI-assisted research is rapidly uncovering Spring vulnerabilities, increasing upgrade pressure. This session explains how Spring teams can respond using Long Term Support releases, Spring Application Advisor for automated CI patching and upgrades, and direct support from the Spring team through VMware Tanzu Spring.

talks.title: The Devoxx Robot Games
talks.abstract: Nine creators showcase AI-assisted games built for Devoxx’s Robot Games challenge at Kinepolis. Each gives a four-minute demo, explaining their tools, AI collaboration, and manual fixes. Expect diverse projects—from Three.js 3D worlds and 2D engines to BBS games, chiptune music, and AI-generated art—then vote for your favorite.

video.title: The Devoxx Robot Games  by Stephan Janssen

talks.title: Who to blame? The AI, The Programmer, or The Prompt?
talks.abstract: An interactive courtroom-style session on AI security, where audiences judge responsibility for five real CVEs in AI tools. It analyzes root causes, evolving vulnerabilities, and the “blame game,” arguing that securing agentic AI requires shared responsibility among developers, providers, and users.

video.title: Who to blame? The AI, The Programmer, or The Prompt?  by Makan Sepehrifar

talks.title: Ask the Architects
talks.abstract: Ask Oracle engineers any questions about your favorite programming language and runtime.

video.title: Ask the Architects  by Gavin Bierman, Maurizio Cimadamore, Per Ake Minborg, Viktor Klang, Alan Batem

talks.title: Building, Shipping and Governing AI Agents on Kubernetes
talks.abstract: A live demo of building and deploying a Kubernetes-based engineering agent with KAgent, AgentGateway, and AgentRegistry. It shows how platform configuration can reduce tool-call overhead, limit context exposure, and enforce least-privilege access without changing agent code.

video.title: Building, Shipping and Governing AI Agents on Kubernetes  by Tom O'Rourke, Ep Heijting

talks.title: Conquest, time travel and explosions using Git
talks.abstract: An interactive talk uses an RTS game built around Git to explain branches, merges, rebases, detached heads, and conflicts. Through time travel, alternate timelines, and explosive gameplay, beginners gain intuition and veterans get a fresh perspective on how Git really works.

video.title: Conquest, time travel and explosions using Git by Alexander Chatzizacharias

talks.title: Hardwood: Building a Parquet Parser From Scratch (With a Little Help From AI)
talks.abstract: A talk about Hardwood, a new modern Java Parquet parser built from scratch to avoid Hadoop dependencies and single-threaded limits. It explores Parquet internals, parallel decoding, high-throughput techniques, JDK Flight Recorder profiling, and lessons from AI-assisted development with Claude Code.

video.title: Hardwood: Building a Parquet Parser From Scratch With a Little Help From AI  by Gunnar Morling

talks.title: Java and the Next Generation of Programming Models
talks.abstract: The session explores using Java to bridge external runtimes and AI models without glue code. It covers the Foreign Function and Memory API and jextract for safe native interaction, then Project Babylon’s code reflection to express, transform, and lower AI models directly in Java for accelerator-backed inference.

video.title: Java and the Next Generation of Programming Models  by Ana Maria Mihalceanu

talks.title: Software engineering in the age of AI agents: who’s in control?
talks.abstract: This talk explores how generative AI is changing software engineering—from coding to verification and guidance. It shares lessons, successes, failures, and responsible practices for using fast-evolving AI tools. The key message: even when AI does the work, humans remain accountable for the outcome.

video.title: Software engineering in the age of AI agents: who’s in control? by Bert Jan Schrijver

talks.title: Taming the Chaos: Security and Predictability in LLM-Powered Applications
talks.abstract: The proposal presents practical patterns for building reliable LLM systems despite inherent randomness. It covers prompt-injection defenses, PII redaction, deterministic validation, self-correction, and multi-model consensus to improve safety and predictability. Examples use Java and LangChain4J, with concepts transferable to other languages and frameworks.

video.title: Taming the Chaos: Security and Predictability in LLM Powered Applications  by Rustam Mehmandarov

talks.title: The Hexagonal Hangover
talks.abstract: The talk critiques dogmatic use of Clean and Hexagonal Architecture, arguing that unnecessary abstraction can hurt code clarity and maintainability. Using Java examples, it explores trade-offs and decision metrics—coupling, cohesion, and distance—to help choose architecture based on context rather than universal “best practices.”

video.title: The Hexagonal Hangover  by Ties van de Ven

talks.title: Beyond the Pod: Architecting and Scaling AI Agents on Kubernetes
talks.abstract: This talk presents Agent Substrate, a Kubernetes system that separates logical AI agents from physical Pods. It enables thousands of stateful, idle agents to share resources efficiently, with hibernation, rapid activation, session teleportation, and dynamic security controls for scalable, isolated AI applications.

video.title: Beyond the Pod: Architecting and Scaling AI Agents on Kubernetes  by Abdellfetah SGHIOUAR

talks.title: Build a private cluster for the office
talks.abstract: A technical talk on building private, local AI systems for regulated organizations using open-weight models. It covers hardware choices, networking, model selection, private data access, and fast document retrieval, helping small teams reduce dependence on frontier model providers while ensuring privacy, governance, and long-term support.

video.title: Build a private cluster for the office by John Davies

talks.title: Faster Development with Java, Python, and Micronaut
talks.abstract: This talk shows how Micronaut, GraalPy, and GraalVM let Python gain Java’s structure, tooling, and native performance without losing simplicity. It explores building polyglot applications, integrating Python and Java cleanly, and using AI to enhance workflows and developer experiences.

video.title: Faster Development with Java, Python, and Micronaut  by Graeme Rocher, Thomas Wuerthinger

talks.title: Kill All Mutants! (Intro to Mutation Testing)
talks.abstract: Mutation testing checks whether tests fail when code is changed, revealing weak tests, redundant or unreachable code. This talk explains how mutation testing works, when to use it, its pros, cons, history, examples, and tools for popular languages.

video.title: Kill All Mutants! Intro to Mutation Testing by Dave Aronson

talks.title: Modernizing legacy code with AI: hands-on examples & lessons learned
talks.abstract: Smals Research shares practical lessons from using AI to modernize legacy software, including Java EE to Jakarta EE migrations and COBOL environments. The session shows where AI speeds up migration, where it fails, and how teams can keep modernization reliable, documented, and verifiable.

video.title: Modernizing legacy code with AI: hands on examples & lessons learned  by Koen Vanderkimpen, Wim Lamb

talks.title: The Dark Secrets of Computer Science
talks.abstract: A humorous talk about the absurdities of software engineering: legacy systems, language quirks, bad integrations, confusing standards, and endless debates like Lombok vs. reactive, CORS, date formats, and vi.
