It riffs on technical pain points, from Y2K38 and IEEE 754 to WASM, Excel, and bizarre HTTP codes.

video.title: The Dark Secrets of Computer Science  by Fabien Marsaud

talks.title: Underneath the Black Marker: AI Techniques for Detecting and Reversing Redactions
talks.abstract: This session demonstrates how redactions fail in PDFs and images, and how AI can recover hidden text or visual content. It also explains proper redaction practices, showing that true privacy requires removing data, not just visually obscuring it.

video.title: Underneath the Black Marker: AI Techniques for Detecting and Reversing Redactions  by David vonThene

talks.title: Why Java Is Perfect for AI - Just Not the AI You’re Thinking Of
talks.abstract: The talk argues that enterprise AI should augment existing Java applications, not replace them. Java’s types, APIs, testing, and concurrency make it well suited to control unpredictable AI outputs, enabling fast, observable, dependable agentic systems without rebuilding architectures or surrendering core business processes.

video.title: Why Java Is Perfect for AI   Just Not the AI You’re Thinking Of  by Trisha Gee, Andrey Santrosyan

talks.title: ADRs: The Why and How
talks.abstract: This presentation explains Architectural Decision Records (ADRs), showing how to create and maintain them and why they matter. It highlights their role in documenting decisions, capturing the reasons behind them, and helping teams reassess choices as business needs or technologies change.

video.title: ADRs: The Why and How  by Venkat Subramaniam

talks.title: Choose your own adventure in agentic design patterns
talks.abstract: This talk explores advanced multi-agent system patterns beyond basics, including routing, swarms, planning approaches, progressive disclosure in skills, LLM-as-Judge evaluation, and agent loops. Drawing on experience with LangChain4j and ADK for Java, it helps developers choose the right abstractions for building effective agentic systems.

video.title: Choose your own adventure in agentic design patterns  by Guillaume Laforge

talks.title: Everyday JSON
talks.abstract: A new JEP proposes a simple, incubating built-in Java API for parsing, navigating, and generating JSON for lightweight use cases where external libraries are unnecessary. The talk explains how Data-Oriented Programming shapes the API, its use cases, trade-offs, and capabilities.

video.title: Everyday JSON by Viktor Klang, Alan Bateman

talks.title: Introducing Agent Control Theory: The System Runs the Model
talks.abstract: The talk presents “Agent Control Theory” for enterprise coding agents: treat agents as measurable systems, log every run, judge against specs, and use evidence to optimize prompts, tools, workflows, or models. It aims to reduce cost, improve quality, and enable vendor portability through controlled experimentation.

video.title: Introducing Agent Control Theory: The System Runs the Model  by Mark Pollack

talks.title: Knocking on the Wrong Door: The Six Developers You’ll Meet in Security
talks.abstract: SECUR-E, an OWASP framework using COM-B, helps teams diagnose why secure development fails—whether due to skills, environment, or motivation—not just awareness. It identifies six developer patterns and guides tailored interventions, improving secure software practices without blame.

video.title: Knocking on the Wrong Door: The Six Developers You’ll Meet in Security  by Enrique Larios Vargas

talks.title: Microservices Without the Distributed Mess
talks.abstract: A pragmatic talk on microservices trade-offs: defining service boundaries, ownership, communication, and consistency using Domain-Driven Design. It explains common pitfalls like distributed monoliths, unclear boundaries, and fragile transactions, and offers practical heuristics for building cohesive, autonomous, understandable services.

video.title: Microservices Without the Distributed Mess  by Steven Hillaert

talks.title: Owning the Code You Didn't Type
talks.abstract: As AI writes code faster than humans can read it, the bottleneck shifts to understanding and accountability. This talk shares practical techniques—phased delivery, guided walk-throughs, human-centered review, engineering depth, and file-based collaboration—to keep developers in control, improve comprehension, and maintain design ownership.

video.title: Owning the Code You Didn't Type by Renato Guerra Cavalcanti

talks.title: Owning the inference layer: When and how to run your own models
talks.abstract: This talk compares hosted model APIs and self-hosted inference for GenAI, covering tradeoffs in cost, latency, flexibility, and data control. It highlights open tools like vLLM and llm-d, and offers a practical framework for deciding when self-hosting is worth the operational complexity.

video.title: Owning the inference layer: When and how to run your own models  by Maarten Vandeperre, Camille Nigo

talks.title: AI in the Dark: Running LLMs in Air-Gapped Production Environments
talks.abstract: This talk describes moving an AI service from demo to production in an air-gapped defence environment with no internet, cloud APIs, or external services. It covers local LLM constraints, offline tool-calling, hallucination risks, and the need for human oversight in a fully isolated system.

video.title: AI in the Dark: Running LLMs in Air Gapped Production Environments by Mihaela Gheorghe Roman

talks.title: Bootiful Security
talks.abstract: Passkeys offer a passwordless future with stronger, simpler authentication. This talk by Daniel Garnier Moiroux and Josh Long explores how Spring Security 7 can help replace passwords, improve security, and streamline login experiences for users and systems.

video.title: Bootiful Security  by Daniel Garnier Moiroux, Josh Long

talks.title: Decoding the Cosmos: Voyager's 1970s Algorithms Meet Today's Cutting-Edge Tech
talks.abstract: This talk explores Voyager’s 1970s-era communication coding, the Viterbi algorithm, and modern machine-learning approaches to decoding deep-space signals. It compares vintage engineering ingenuity with today’s tools through real examples and demonstrations, showing how classic algorithms and AI can help process interstellar data.

video.title: Decoding the Cosmos: Voyager's 1970s Algorithms Meet Today's Cutting Edge Tech  by Pieter van der Me

talks.title: From a startup stack to 5 microseconds: inside a crypto trading engine
talks.abstract: Bitvavo rebuilt its live crypto exchange core for deterministic, replayable, low-latency processing. Replacing database-centered architecture with an ordered log, replicated state machine, Raft, and reliable UDP delivered sub-millisecond latency and 100,000 orders/second, while balancing correctness, operational complexity, and JVM performance constraints.

video.title: From a startup stack to 5 microseconds: inside a crypto trading engine  by Oleg Lobanov

talks.title: Help! I hate my team mate!
talks.abstract: The talk explores common team conflicts when new members join or working styles clash, leading to mistrust, disrespect, and demotivation. It shares real experiences and practical ways teams handle these problems, helping participants understand their options when cooperation breaks down.

video.title: Help! I hate my team mate! by Jessica Siewert

talks.title: Production-Ready Java Containers: Smaller, Faster, Smarter
talks.abstract: This session explores optimizing Java containers using tailored runtimes with jlink, CDS, AOT, JVM container awareness, memory tuning, and efficient image-building practices. Through progressive measurement, it examines trade-offs among size, startup, warmup, memory, throughput, observability, security, and maintainability to support informed, workload-specific engineering decisions.

video.title: Production Ready Java Containers: Smaller, Faster, Smarter  by Albert Attard

talks.title: Their API Went Down. So Why Is My App on Fire?
talks.abstract: The talk explains how to protect your app from outages in APIs you don’t control. Beyond try-except, it covers practical patterns like caching 429s, resuming syncs, and using circuit breakers to prevent external failures from cascading into your own production system.

video.title: Their API Went Down  So Why Is My App on Fire?  by Ines Panker

talks.title: Open Source in the Age of AI: Where's the value?
talks.abstract: This talk explores how AI changes the value of open source, asking whether libraries and tools remain commercially useful when AI can generate code. It brings together maintainers and contributors to discuss funding, community, business models, and the purpose of open source in an AI-driven world.

talks.title: What Does it Print? The Java Quiz (Hard Edition 🤯)
talks.abstract: Interactive Java session exploring tricky language subtleties through short code snippets. Participants will predict outputs together, revisit core concepts, challenge assumptions, and deepen their understanding of how Java actually behaves in practice.

talks.title: F*ck The System, and other bad ideas for the future
talks.abstract: A provocative manifesto exploring today’s geopolitical upheaval and asking how Europe can become sovereign, resilient, and innovative in the emerging world order. It challenges old assumptions, reimagines the future, and appeals to citizens, entrepreneurs, policymakers, and thinkers seeking a stronger Europe.

video.title: F*ck The System, and other bad ideas for the future by Jo Caudron

talks.title: All you need to know about Maven 4!
talks.abstract: This talk explores Maven 4’s long-awaited development, the challenges of evolving a mature ecosystem without breaking compatibility, and the motivations behind its redesign. It also highlights key new features and improvements in the upcoming major release.

video.title: All you need to know about Maven 4!  by Matthias Bünger

talks.title: Escaping Java's Allocation Gravity with Value Classes
talks.abstract: This talk introduces Java’s Project Valhalla value types through a black hole simulation, showing how they improve immutability, memory efficiency, and performance for heavy numerical workloads. It also explores experimental non-nullable `!` syntax, optimization potential, current limitations, and practical benchmarks.

video.title: Escaping Java's Allocation Gravity with Value Classes By Clément de Tastes, Remi Forax

talks.title: In the loop, not in the dark: staying in control in the era of dark software factories
talks.abstract: After Backlog.md enabled agents to generate 300,000 lines with limited oversight, Groma.md restores architectural ownership. It maintains a real-time project blueprint as the source of truth, guiding agent-driven implementation while keeping humans focused on meaningful design decisions. A live demonstration will map a large open-source repository into Groma.

video.title: In the loop , not in the dark: Staying in controlling the era dark software factories   By Alex Gavr

talks.title: The Quantum Tech Lead: Hands-On and Abstract at the Same Time
talks.abstract: This talk explores the transition from individual contributor to technical leader, showing how leadership can amplify impact rather than reduce it. Drawing on experience at CERN, it shares practical techniques for adapting, staying relevant, and maintaining technical influence while leading teams.

video.title: The Quantum Tech Lead: Hands On and Abstract at the Same Time  by Cristian Schuszter

talks.title: Why it takes 3000 commits to bring Valhalla's value objects to the JDK
talks.abstract: JEP 401 Value Objects arrives in OpenJDK preview, enabling a new Java type model with minimal code changes. The talk explains what value objects are, JVM benefits, Valhalla history, implementation details, and the path toward bridging objects and primitives, including future support like `List<int>`.

video.title: Why it takes 3000 commits to bring Valhalla's value objects to the JDK by David Simms

talks.title: 10 Billion Records vs. The Regulator: An Architectural Post-Mortem of an 11TB Exadata Failure
talks.abstract: A major bank incident triggered a BaFin investigation after an 11TB Oracle Exadata system failed at 10 billion records. This session examines emergency mitigation, a missed query-window check, cache warming, shifting deduplication to writes, and designing zero-loss dual-write migration to Cloud PostgreSQL.

video.title: 10 Billion Records vs  The Regulator: An Architectural Post Mortem of an 11TB Exadata Failure  by Ma

talks.title: Embabel Agent v1.5
talks.abstract: Embabel is a JVM-native agent framework built on Spring AI and Spring Boot that replaces LLM-driven decision-making with deterministic Goal-Oriented Action Planning (GOAP). Developers declare goals and actions; a code-generated planner chains them by conditions, producing inspectable, reproducible, and explainable execution traces.

video.title: Embabel Agent v1 5 By Rod Johnson

talks.title: Is AI killing XP practices? (Or are we letting it?)
talks.abstract: AI can tempt teams to skip core XP practices like TDD, refactoring, pair programming, and CI. This session shows why these habits are at risk in AI-assisted development, what breaks when they’re ignored, and why they matter even more as AI accelerates both good and bad engineering.

video.title: Is AI killing XP practices? Or are we letting it? By Nacho Cougil

talks.title: What’s happening with Project Amber?
talks.abstract: Project Amber is advancing Java’s data-oriented programming with new pattern-matching features: user-defined deconstruction, nested constant patterns, exhaustive matching, safer primitive conversions, and compact record reconstruction. The talk explores experimental designs, their benefits, and the language design challenges they introduce.

video.title: What’s happening with Project Amber? By Gavin Bierman

talks.title: You thought technical debt was bad? Meet design debt!
talks.abstract: The talk argues that technical debt is only the surface of deeper accidental design debt, which can worsen despite best practices like refactoring, KISS, and YAGNI. It explores how design debt forms, affects architecture and business, and how to detect, assess, and prevent it.

video.title: You thought technical debt was bad? Meet design debt!  by Julien Topçu, Josian Chevalier

talks.title: 10 boring reasons why Java is the best ecosystem for agentic development
talks.abstract: The talk argues that Java’s “boring” strengths—types, tests, static analysis, mature builds, formatting, observability, and more—help control AI agents’ risks like hallucinations, non-determinism, and unmaintainable code. It maps 10 Java features to agent failure modes and ends with a practical agent-safe checklist.

video.title: 10 boring reasons why Java is the best ecosystem for agentic development By Ed Burns

talks.title: Java Next - From Valhalla to Leyden, from Babylon to Panama, from Amber to Detroit
talks.abstract: This talk explores Java’s evolution and future through major projects: Valhalla’s unified type system, Leyden’s faster startup, Babylon’s foreign models and hardware support, Panama’s native interoperability, Amber’s expressive language features, Loom’s structured concurrency, and Detroit’s Python/JavaScript integration. Attendees will gain a roadmap of Java’s coming years.

video.title: Java Next   From Valhalla to Leyden, from Babylon to Panama, from Amber to Detroit By Nicolai Parlog

talks.title: My old trains have a second life, with TinyGo!
talks.abstract: A retro model train hobby project was modernized with Seeed Studio hardware, Bluetooth, and TinyGo to create a digital railway network with individual train control for speed, direction, and lights. The talk covers embedded hardware/software architecture, lessons learned, and open-source implementation.

video.title: My old trains have a second life, with TinyGo! By Florian FORESTIER, Justine Bachelard

talks.title: Strangling the dragon: modernizing legacy systems with the Strangler Fig pattern
talks.abstract: The talk argues against full rewrites of legacy systems, citing risk and the second system effect. It promotes the Strangler Fig pattern for gradual replacement, combined with Domain-Driven Design and the Inverse Conway Manoeuvre to align system architecture with team structure.

video.title: Strangling the dragon: modernizing legacy systems with the Strangler Fig pattern   by Daniel Ranela

talks.title: We created our own AI orchestrator and it became so much more!
talks.abstract: We built an agent orchestration tool using Embabel Agent, Skills, and Spec files to coordinate AI-driven software work. It provides a visual dashboard for active agents, tasks, and next steps, reshaping team roles: developers review AI output, analysts define requirements, and product owners manage faster sprint queues.

video.title: We created our own AI orchestrator and it became so much more!  by Ricky van Rijn
